claims.claim: **Suspect an effusion in any unwell child with pneumonia, or when fever persists despite 48 hours of appropriate antibiotics.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Simple** effusion = sterile, non-loculated transudate. **Complicated** = loculated effusion or empyema, from bacterial invasion of the pleural space.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Commonest empyema organisms:** *S. pneumoniae*, *S. aureus* and Group A Streptococcus.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On examination:** localised absent breath sounds with a dull percussion note, alongside the adjacent pneumonia's bronchial breathing and crackles.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severity depends on the child's clinical state, not the size or look of the effusion.** Severe features: marked tachycardia, altered mental state, severe respiratory distress, cyanosis or severe hypoxaemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other causes to consider:** TB or mycoplasma, malignancy, foreign body, congestive cardiac failure, rheumatological serositis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No laboratory test is diagnostic.** Consider FBE, UEC (think SIADH and atypical HUS), CRP (tracks treatment success) and blood culture.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severely unwell:** LFTs (albumin) and coagulation studies — consider toxic shock syndrome.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If a drain goes in,** think about sending the pleural fluid for MC&S, Gram stain and pneumococcal PCR.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Imaging:** AP CXR; **chest ultrasound distinguishes simple from complicated.** CT is not routine — only for failure to respond or suspected malignancy or foreign body.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Outpatient management is possible** for a small simple effusion with no respiratory distress in a child tolerating oral antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Admit** when respiratory support is needed (hypoxia, work of breathing moderate to severe), hydration support, IV antibiotics, or to assess the effusion's severity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Restrict maintenance NG or IV fluids to 2/3rds of calculated requirement** to avoid fluid overload, with regular review of fluid status.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Supportive care:** oxygen if required, analgesia, encourage mobilisation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Antibiotics: a 3rd generation cephalosporin first line; consider MSSA and MRSA cover.** Definitive therapy follows investigation results and local specialist advice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discuss with the local paediatric team** any child with an effusion who needs admission.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss with respiratory and/or surgical team:** complicated effusion · septic shock (a drain may be needed for source control) · severe respiratory distress · fever or respiratory distress persisting beyond 48hrs of IV antimicrobials.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer:** complicated effusion where surgery is anticipated · cardiac, chronic respiratory, immunodeficiency or immunosuppression comorbidity · high-level respiratory support · care beyond the local hospital's comfort level.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** tolerating oral antibiotics, afebrile, off oxygen and tolerating adequate oral intake.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Parapneumonic effusion' (Last updated August 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Parapneumonic_effusion/, retrieved 2026-09-23
